entry.content:
Vigilante transformed a Texas-sourced 1979 Wagoneer into a black-on-black statement with a whiskey-colored leather cabin. The chrome is matte black, the glass is smoked, and the leather is paired with the Wagoneer's corduroy. Even the woodgrain on its sides is recolored after shou sugi ban, the Japanese technique of charring wood. A 392 Hemi V8 engine makes 485 horsepower, and 4-wheel drive lets the Wagoneer handle icy conditions or rougher terrain. The window cranks look original but operate like electric windows. This example is sold, but consider it a teaser of Vigilante's made-to-order work: you pick the colors, drivetrain, and wheels.

Classic motorcycle racing jackets earned their character through years of wear, but this version arrives with the hard work already done. Cut from 100% sheep leather, the Line of Trade Leather Riders Jacket undergoes a washing process that gives the hide a supple feel and rich, broken-in appearance from the first wear. A two-way front zipper accommodates changing layers, while zippered chest and lower pockets keep essentials secure. Vented snap cuffs, traditional back seaming, and a one-piece collar with a half-moon stand preserve the jacket's racing heritage. A cotton twill lining completes the comfortable, lived-in construction.

entry.title: 1977 Land Rover 101 Forward Control Survival Truck
entry.summary: The Land Rover 101 Forward Control was designed in the Cold War for one job: hauling the British Army's L118 Light Gun, plus a ton of shells and kit, over any terrain. The Army is said to have wanted a truck small enough to fly in a cargo plane, so engineers placed the cab over t
entry.content:
The Land Rover 101 Forward Control was designed in the Cold War for one job: hauling the British Army's L118 Light Gun, plus a ton of shells and kit, over any terrain. The Army is said to have wanted a truck small enough to fly in a cargo plane, so engineers placed the cab over the front axle, tucked a 3.5-liter Rover V8 behind it, and named the truck for its 101-inch wheelbase. Locking differentials and four-wheel drive pulled it through mud, the body panels reportedly came off for helicopter lifts, and some chassis ended up as ambulances and radio trucks. About 2,650 were built by 1978 and many served into the 1990s. Private buyers could get them only as military surplus, and civilians today drive them as survival trucks, like this 1977 truck, which sold at auction.

entry.title: Lebond x Norman Foster Natural Titanium Watch
entry.summary: Norman Foster, the Pritzker Prize-winning architect behind London's Gherkin, Apple Park and the Reichstag dome in Berlin, designed his first watch at 91 with the Swiss maker Lebond. A pilot with a long history of travel, he gave it a bezel that rotates both ways to track a second
entry.content:
Norman Foster, the Pritzker Prize-winning architect behind London's Gherkin, Apple Park and the Reichstag dome in Berlin, designed his first watch at 91 with the Swiss maker Lebond. A pilot with a long history of travel, he gave it a bezel that rotates both ways to track a second time zone. Foster chose Grade 5 titanium for the 38.5mm case to cut weight without losing strength. He also removed the lugs, the arms that normally hold a strap, so the case and the light grey rubber strap read as one continuous shape around the wrist. A custom blue rotor, the part that winds the watch, shows through the sapphire caseback. Each case is individually numbered.
